title: La cuenta dividida en el café de Madrid

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.spanish: Oye, Pablo, el camarero dice que no nos divide la cuenta en la terraza.
dialogue.english: Hey, Pablo, the waiter says he won't split the bill for us on the patio.

dialogue.speaker: Pablo
dialogue.spanish: ¡Qué fuerte! Bueno, no pasa nada, pago yo todo con tarjeta porque andas sin pasta.
dialogue.english: That's wild! Well, no worries, I'll pay the whole thing by card since you're out of cash.

slang.actualMeaning: money / cash (very common slang across Spain)
slang.example: No salgo este finde porque no tengo nada de pasta.

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.spanish: Mil gracias, tío. Te hago un Bizum de doce euros ahora mismo por mis tostadas y el cortado.
dialogue.english: Thanks a million, dude. I'll send you a 12-euro Bizum transfer right now for my toast and espresso.

slang.actualMeaning: dude / mate / guy (everyday Spanish friend address)

dialogue.speaker: Pablo
dialogue.spanish: Vale, genial. Vámonos pitando que el metro cierra en veinte minutos.
dialogue.english: Okay, great. Let's get out of here fast because the metro closes in twenty minutes.

slang.actualMeaning: in a big hurry / right away (irse pitando)
slang.example: Salí pitando de la oficina para no perder el tren.

questions.question: What problem do Carmen and Pablo run into at the Madrid café?
options: The waiter says he won't split the bill on the patio
The credit card machine is broken
The kitchen ran out of toast and coffee
They forgot their phones at home
questions.explanation: Carmen says: 'el camarero dice que no nos divide la cuenta en la terraza' (the waiter won't split the bill).

questions.question: How does Carmen pay Pablo back for her share?
options: She gives him a 20-euro bill in cash
She sends him a 12-euro Bizum mobile transfer
She buys his metro ticket at the station
She promises to buy breakfast tomorrow
questions.explanation: Carmen says: 'Te hago un Bizum de doce euros ahora mismo por mis tostadas y el cortado.'

questions.question: Why do they need to leave the café quickly at the end?
options: It is starting to rain on the patio
They have a movie reservation at eight
The café is closing its terrace
questions.explanation: Pablo says: 'Vámonos pitando que el metro cierra en veinte minutos.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: When Pablo says 'andas sin pasta' and 'vámonos pitando', what do 'pasta' and 'irse pitando' mean in Spain?
options: 'Pasta' = money/cash; 'irse pitando' = to leave in a hurry
'Pasta' = Italian food; 'irse pitando' = to whistle a song
'Pasta' = patience; 'irse pitando' = to take a taxi
'Pasta' = battery; 'irse pitando' = to argue with the waiter
questions.explanation: In Spain, 'pasta' is slang for money/cash, and 'irse pitando' means to leave in a rush!
